IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: HROS will provide high spectral resolution data in the optical range, suitable for detailed study of stars, quasars, and planet radial velocity programs.
[REQ-0-SRD-1630] R~20,000 (1-2.5 µm ); R~100,000 (3-5 µm )
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0080] The average power dissipated per actuator during operations, excluding the embedded SCC electronics, shall be less than 1.55 W. [REQ-2-M1CS-0160]
Gamma-ray bursts

Discussion: This corresponds to the value in the power budget [RD 17], and includes 0.7 W from the encoder and interpolator, 0.6 W from the offloader motor, 0.1 W from the voice coil, 0.05 W for the snubber and its sensor, and 0.1 W for other functions. It excludes the power dissipated by the embedded SCC electronics. This requirement is the average over time and over the set of actuators, i.e., higher peak powers are allowed, and actuators with higher power dissipation can be offset by actuators with lower power dissipation.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0110] The actuator shall meet all performance requirements over the environmental range shown in Table 1, Column (B). [REQ-2-M1CS-0340]
Variation of fundamental physical constants

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0150] The actuator shall meet all performance requirements when oriented at all angles between vertical (0 deg) and 79 deg, and at all orientations about the output shaft axis. [REQ-2-M1CS-0800]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0060] The total mass of the M1CS actuator, output flexure rod, and any mounting hardware to attach the actuator to the fixed frame, excluding the embedded SCC electronics, shall not exceed 13 kg per actuator. [REQ-2-M1CS-0100]
Lyman-alpha power spectrum

ReqIF_Properties_Profile:ObjectPropertie.Comments: WFOS, same requirements as for baryonic power spectrum for the nature of dark matter

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: [REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0160] The actuator, when de-energized, shall maintain its position with a deadband of 0.8 mm (i.e., +/‑0.4 mm) for all elevation angles and the full range of loads in REQ-2-M1CS-1020. [REQ-2-M1CS-0840,-0430]
Tidal Flares
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0115] The actuator shall remain functional in order to support servicing and maintenance over the environmental range shown in Table 1, Column (C). [REQ-2-M1CS-0300]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0208] The actuator, in any installed state, shall survive a sinusoidal force applied to the output with peak amplitude of 3600 N (TBC), added to a static load of 0 to 730 N, at frequencies between 0 and 15 Hz (TBC). [REQ-2-M1CS-0427]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0200] The actuators shall be designed such that while in any installed state (operating or non-operating) and any orientation they shall survive earthquakes up to the levels of the 10-year-return period earthquake with no damage. [REQ-2-M1CS-0420].

Discussion: The telescope must be able to point to the horizon for servicing. As the segments themselves follow the curvature of the primary mirror, they may be tilted as much as an additional 14 deg from the telescope optical axis.
This requirement addresses the case where the telescope is moved with the actuators off, including to horizon, where some of the actuators will see a negative (“pull”) load. The actuator would not be actively driven. In this case, the actuator motion would be constrained by the snubber. The range of motion is the same as that given in REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0230. Meeting REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0230, which has larger loads, will ensure that this requirement is met.
As a goal, the actuator shall remain functional in order to support servicing and maintenance over actuator zenith angles from 0 to 104 deg.
Baryonic power spectrum
Discussion: These requirements describe the load capacity of the actuator to survive earthquake disturbances.
Galactic Center

ReqIF_Properties_Profile:ObjectPropertie.Comments: Ideally IRIS but WIRC will do for imaging part

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: Discussion: The derivation of the loads on the actuator is described in RD‎9. The 1000 yr amplitude assumes a 3 g peak excitation applied to the actuator base, and 57% as much for the 200 yr earthquake. The frequency content comes from the mirror cell response for the 2008 DSL design to the Gemini input spectrum. A simple model of the snubber with a dead zone per REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0230 is used.
Discussion: These values will remain TBC pending more definitive end-to-end modeling of the disturbance, the final telescope structure, the SSA, and actuator with snubber.

Discussion: This requirement describes the startup and shutdown (intentional or not) behavior of the actuator. The 1 g force limit is a fraction of the 3 g minimum design load of the optical system. This is value is more than 10x the dynamical force requirement in REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0680, and the requirement will be achieved by practical current limits in the SCC implementation.

Discussion: Requirement 0210 accommodates the 200 yr and shorter return period earthquakes. It corresponds to +/- 2.8g at the actuator output with respect to its nominal 74 kg inertial load. While recovery time before the resumption of observing is allowed for the 200 yr earthquake, because of the large number of actuators, we adopt here that there be no damage.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0230] The actuator, in any installed state, shall limit its total instantaneous range of travel to 0.8 mm (i.e., +/‑0.4 mm), when subject to a load of +/‑1000 N applied to the output. [REQ-2-M1CS-0430]

Discussion: Requirement 0208 accommodates the 1000 yr return period earthquake in order to prevent actuator failure from causing severe optics damage. It corresponds to +/- 5g at the actuator output with respect to its nominal 74 kg inertial load. Actuator damage may occur, i.e., loads could exceed YS, but must stay below UTS, unless a caging mechanism is incorporated.

Discussion: The electrical aspects of the ICD are still TBD. In the SCC conceptual architecture, the actuator drive and interface electronics will be collocated with the actuator inside its enclosure, and the actuator mechanical envelope will include adequate volume. The electrical interface to the actuator is expected to be via a single weatherproof connector on the housing.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0290] The actuator shall be designed, while in any state, to survive without damage repeated exposure to the environmental Survival Conditions shown in Table 1, Column (D). [REQ-2-M1CS-0410]

Discussion: The telescope must be able to observe anywhere on the sky from 1 to 65 deg zenith angle. As the segments follow the curvature of the primary mirror, the actuator tilt varies across the mirror. As the actuators are mounted parallel to the segment normal, for the 30 m circumscribed telescope diameter and a face-to-face segment diameter of 1.24 m, the maximum effective actuator radius is 14.4 m. For a 60 m ROC, actuators at the edge are canted in by up to arcsin(14.4/60) = 14 deg.

Discussion: Note that we assume for now that with integral actuator electronics, that the actuator with its internal electronics is a single field-replaceable unit. This approach would allow for internal actuator devices to be pre-connectorized with standard PCB-style connectors, improving modularity and avoiding an extra cable harness. The PCB could also be used to mount limit switches.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_2100000140_280000009d__46fbb024-41ff-4372-939c-391230de10c4_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
Discussion: This ICD documents the attachment of the actuator to the SSA at the fixed frame and at the moving frame, developed jointly by the optics and actuator groups.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0400] The actuator shall conform to the mechanical interface requirements defined in the M1CS Actuator Interface Control Document, including attachment to SSA fixed and moving frames for both sector clockings.

Discussion: We adopt the 0.8 mm requirement from RD‎8 which assumed 1 g rms disturbances. For a sinusoidal disturbance, peak forces are ~1000 N for the nominal 74 kg inertial mass. This requirement could be achieved with an unloaded dead-zone of +/‑0.25 mm, and end-stop compliance of 10 N/um.

Discussion: The actuators should not need complicated external command sequences for initialization. 5 minutes is an adopted value. Note that it takes 2.8 minutes to slew over the full range at the rate specified by REQ-2-M1CS-0640.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0440] The actuator shall have an automated initialization procedure which can be completed in less than 5 minutes. [REQ-2-M1CS-2345]

Discussion: This is a derived requirement: the OAD only specifies the actuator range and SSA compliance with that range. The current range of travel of the SSA, as limited by its locks, is +/‑3 mm for a pure piston move (i.e., for all three PSA actuators moving together). Note that the SSA locks are at a smaller radius than the actuators, and thus do not limit tilt very well: hence the requirement.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0420] The actuator shall include stops that limit its maximum travel to no more than +/- 3 mm. The actuator shall not be damaged, or require manual recovery, if driven into its stops. [REQ-2-M1CS-0430]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0210] The actuator, in any installed state, shall survive without damage a sinusoidal force applied to the output with peak amplitude of 2000 N (TBC), added to a static load of 0 to 730 N, at frequencies between 0 and 15 Hz (TBC). [REQ-2-M1CS-0427]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0620] The actuator shall have a minimum operational stroke of 5.0 mm. [REQ-2-M1CS-2400]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0280] The actuator, on loss or restoration of power, shall limit peak forces to 1 g. [REQ-2-M1CS-0460]

Discussion: The rate uses an adopted load change of 750 N; see the discussion following REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1000. We adopt 60 sec, as in REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0640. For reference, for a soft actuator with an offload compliance of 175,000 N/m, this corresponds to 70 um/sec applied to the offload spring (achieved at 3.6 rps with an 18:1 gearbox, 12 tpi screw, and a 6:1 offload ratio).
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0640] The actuator shall have a minimum position slew rate of 30 micron/sec. [REQ-2-M1CS-0870, -0872]

Discussion: For the mirror cell design as of 5/27/2008 [RD5] the maximum actuator rate (between 60 and 65 deg) is 40.4 micron/deg. REQ-1-ORD-2710 states that the system shall be able to guide with a speed up to 1.1 times the sidereal rate, or 16.5 deg/hr, yielding 185 nm/sec. The max deflection from RD5 is 1.64 mm; we scale this to 1.8 mm per REQ-1-OAD-0800. With these two factors, the maximum rate is 200 nm/sec. We apply 30% margin, in part to accommodate dynamical requirements.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0660] The actuator shall be able to track at position rates up to 260 nm/sec. [REQ-2-M1CS-0866]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0670] The actuator shall be able to track at quasistatic force rates up to 0.08 N/sec. [REQ-2-M1CS-0866]

Discussion: This is a requirement on the instantaneous force output from the soft actuator. Based on modeling (see the discussion below REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1040), peak forces of 2 N are required to accommodate wind disturbances. The larger value, here, allows use of the voice-coil stage only for extended periods of time. Assuming a 30 N/√W motor constant referred to the output, +/-40 N requires 1.8W, max., or an average of 0.6 W for a linear ramp of force over the full range. Using the value from REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0670, such a force range would allow ~1000 s between offloads in the worse case; ~2000 s for more typical actuators and zenith angles. For reference, per the power budget in REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0080, the 0.1 W allocated to the voice coil corresponds to 10 N rms for a 30 N/√W motor constant referred to the output.

Discussion: This value corresponds to the change in actuator force for an elevation rate of 16.5 deg/hr, and the maximum inertial load of 84 kg from REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1010. This requirement is additional to REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0660, which specifies the position rate.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0680] The actuator shall be able to produce dynamical forces of up to +/-40 N peak. [REQ-2-M1CS-0874, -0876]

Discussion: This requirement also addresses the need to support small moves. As described in RD18, ~23 N peak force is required in the worst case, i.e., the actuator must remain linear for forces to this value. We adopt the larger value in the requirement, as discussed above.

Discussion: This requirement addresses the case where the actuator is powered down at one elevation and then powered up and initialized at another. By specifying the performance range, this requirement assumes that the telescope is moved to an elevation angle of at least 65 deg before initializing the actuator.
Discussion: The performance impacts of transients are described in more detail in RD12. The rms contribution of transients is included in EQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0700.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0710] The maximum absolute actuator tracking error shall be less than or equal to 50 nm. [REQ-2-M1CS-3200]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0430] The actuator shall not be damaged if it encounters an external hard stop within its range of travel. [REQ-2-M1CS-0430]
Discussion: Note that if the actuator is incorrectly mounted, or the SSA locks are not released, the SSA locks could limit actuator travel before the actuator reached its internal hard stops.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0730] Offloads must be completed in 5 sec or less.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0300] The actuator shall conform to the electrical interface requirements defined in the M1CS Actuator Interface Control Document, including provision for incorporating the drive electronics inside the actuator housing, and providing a weatherproof electrical connector.

Discussion: This value is equal to the “actuator noise” component in the PSSN allocation for “Segment Dynamic Displacement Residual” [RD14]. The adopted high-pass filter is intended to provide a conservative model of the performance of the global control loop, which will correct low-frequency actuator errors. This term includes only errors produced by sources in the actuator as mounted on a fixed base, and excludes wind disturbances and other external sources of error.
Discussion: The baseline implementation is the output encoder, although retain for now the stiffness requirement for the collocated encoder.
Discussion: This requirement affects wind rejection; see the discussion at the beginning of this section (‎3.4.3).
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0805] The actuator and output flexure shall have an axial stiffness of no less than 9.0 N/micron at dc (0 Hz) when mounted to the SSA. [REQ-2-M1CS-3160]

Discussion: The static actuator compliance includes three terms: the mechanism compliance; the compliance of the output flexure that connects the actuator to the moving frame; and additional compliance associated with the interfaces to the SSA. For the collocated encoder, based on current testing, these terms are approximately 14 N/um (limited by the flex pivots), 60 N/um, and 60 N/um (adopt 9 N/um for this configuration). With the output encoder, for which the mechanism compliance is inside of the closed loop, only the last two terms contribute (adopt 20 N/um for this configuration).
Discussion: These four requirements apply to a discrete-offload actuator, and are described in RD12 , as presented to the SAC. This type of actuator is not currently baselined.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0700] [REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0700] The rms actuator tracking error in any 1 minute window at frequencies above 0.25 Hz shall be less than or equal to 4.4 nm. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0820] The stiffness of the actuator when mounted on a rigid base shall be no less than 0.3 N/um between 10 and 20 Hz. [REQ-2-M1CS-3162]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0720] The actuator must be able to track within spec for at least 15 minutes between any offloads.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0812] The actuator, when mounted to the SSA, shall limit the amplification of disturbances between the actuator attachment point on the fixed frame to the mirror surface to less than a factor of 5 over the frequency range of 25‑40 Hz. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]

Discussion: The specified slew rate corresponds to 1.8 mm travel in 60 sec. The range is the gravity deflection term in the actuator travel budget, REQ-1-OAD-0800. The duration is chosen as a fraction of the 3 minutes allowed in REQ-1-ORD-1800 for the telescope and enclosure to be able to point from any one position on the sky to any other and settle control loops and structural dynamics sufficiently to be ready for object acquisition.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0740] The actuator must have a continuous range between offloads of 175 um.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0450] The actuator shall be able to be initialized starting from any position in its operational stroke and for any load in the performance range. [REQ-2-M1CS-2345]

Discussion: This value is explicitly called out in the OAD: REQ-1-OAD-0808. Of this, 1.8 mm is allocated for gravity deflection and 0.42 mm for thermal deformation, with the remainder allocated for installation errors, diagnostics, and margin. The actuator physical travel, as limited by its hard stops, REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0420, may be larger than this range, but performance beyond this range is not required.
Discussion: Passive damping is necessary in order to design a controller with adequate SISO gain and phase margins in the presence of SSA resonances and CSI; see RD7.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0800] The actuator, when mounted on a rigid base, shall be capable of achieving an axial stiffness of 2.5 N/micron at 1 Hz and below. [REQ-2-M1CS-3166]

Discussion: See RD13 and RD7, and the discussion at the beginning of this section (3.4.3). From the technology downselect, a gain of less than 5 (system damping >10%) is required to provide acceptable PSSN in the presence of vibration. For a soft actuator, this is achieved through its natural isolation properties. For a hard actuator, it would likely need to be provided through active damping.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0850] Soft actuator only: The soft actuator must provide passive damping of at least 5000 N/(m/s) with a 3 dB frequency of at least 50 Hz over the full range of travel. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]
REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0855] Soft actuator only: The open-loop reflected mass of the actuator shall be between 30 and 60 kg. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0650] The actuator shall have a minimum force slew rate of 12.5 N/sec. [REQ-2-M1CS-0870, -0872]

Discussion: the value of the offload compliance plays a role in the control modeling and system design. An actuator with this value of compliance is able to achieve adequate performance per the discussion at the beginning of this section (3.4.3). Note: this offload compliance includes the contribution of the offload springs and residual compliance of the flexures. For calculating force rates, only the offload spring stiffness is used.
Discussion: This requirement affects the rejection of acoustic disturbance; see the discussion at the beginning of this section (3.4.3). These are described as guidelines in OAD.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0752] It must be possible to synchronize offloads, and to coordinate offloads with AO and other instruments.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0900] The actuator shall support a servo update rate of up to 50 Hz. [REQ-2-M1CS-3140]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0830] The stiffness of the actuator when mounted on a rigid base shall be no less than (11-f)/10 N/micron for frequencies between 1 and 10 Hz. [REQ-2-M1CS-3164]
Discussion: All actuator concepts require an encoder in order to provide the required performance. This requirement formalizes the need to make this data available externally.

Discussion for REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0800 through -0865
The requirements in this section largely affect the PSSN for “Segment Dynamic Displacement Residual” in response to wind and vibration disturbances (REQ-2-M1CS-3000). Document RD19 provides the basis for many of these values, based on current disturbance and system modeling, as well as on test data from the P2 actuator attached to the P1 SSA. The modeling also accounts for CSI, which constrains the servo gain that can be applied when the actuators are mounted on the telescope, vs. on a rigid base.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0914] The actuator shall provide burst-mode position telemetry at up to 1000 Hz for diagnostics. [REQ-2-M1CS-2560, -2630]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0910] The actuator shall provide continuous position telemetry at up to 50 Hz. [REQ-2-M1CS-2560]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0940] The actuator shall be designed to meet all requirements when incorporated into the telescope dynamical model, including the effect of SSA and mirror cell dynamics, and control-structure-interaction (CSI) issues. [REQ-2-M1CS-0420]
Discussion: This requirement affects the rejection of acoustic disturbance; see the discussion at the beginning of this section (3.4.3). These are described as guidelines in OAD.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1010] The actuator shall meet all performance requirements with an inertial mass of 70 to 81 kg. [REQ-2-M1CS-0800]

Discussion: This requirement is to ensure that the actuator will meet requirements when it is mounted on the SSA in the full telescope structure. The implications of this requirement are specific to the actuator technology, and need to be worked with the TMT control group. The M1CS parent requirement specifies the PSSN for the Segment Dynamic Displacement residual.
Discussion: As a goal, the actuator shall function with smoothly degraded performance over that axial load range.
Discussion: This requirement supports sys ID for actuator tuning. It does not have to be real-time.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1020] The actuator shall maintain position as described in REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0160 with an axial load ranging from -280 N to 920 N. [REQ-2-M1CS-0840]

Discussion for -1000 through -1040:
The current best estimate (CBE) for the PSA moving mass is 215.9 kg [RD10, last updated 12/4/2012] with an uncertainty of 5%. Per the M1CS mass budget [RD16, last updated 01/08/2013], 3.4 kg is allocated for 12 sensor blocks and boots, and 3 kg for 4 electronic boxes and 1 cable assembly. This yields a total moving mass of 222 kg, or 74 kg per actuator. We adopt -5%/+10% uncertainty, for a range of moving mass of 70 to 81 kg, or a zenith force of 690 to 790 N, with a nominal of 725 N.
The measured P1 guide flexure force is +102 / -163 N at an extension of ±2.54 mm [RD11]. From the P2 flexure modeling [RD15], the expected force is +106 / ‑189 N at ±2.55 mm (and +143 / -269 N at ±3 mm). We adopt the P2 values, corresponding to +35 / -63 N per actuator. As the actuator range of travel budget [AD2, Table 12] already includes 2.33 (out of 5 mm) total travel margin, we don’t add additional margin to the guide flexure force.
The maximum disturbance force is approximately ±2 N per actuator. This corresponds to a 3.5 Pa wind force from a 3 m/s wind perpendicular to the segment, divided among the three actuators, and is reasonable worst case from aero-optical modeling as of Jan 2013. (F = 0.5ρV2A for ρ =0.78 kg/m3 at the summit, V=3 m/s, and A = 1.35 m2).
All requirements must be met for telescope zenith angles between 0 and 65 deg, or because of the curvature of the primary, actuator zenith angles 0 and 79 deg, or loads between 100% and 19% of the zenith load.
Thus, the maximum performance load is 790+35+2 = 830 N. The minimum performance load is 0.19×690‑63-2 =130 – 65 = 65 N.
In the current design, the residual stiffness of the 4-bar linkage is 22 N/mm. Thus, in the worse case with actuator retracted by 2.5 mm, the offloader is just preloaded by 10 N.
The actuator must maintain position for telescope zenith angles between 0 and 90 deg, or because of the curvature of the primary, actuator zenith angles 0 and 104 deg, or loads between 100% and -24% of the zenith load.
For the maximum functional load, we an additional 10% margin to the maximum performance load, yielding 920 N.
For the minimum functional load, this yields ‑0.24×790‑65 N, to which we add additional 10 % margin, yielding -280 N.
The measured P1 guide flexure stiffness [RD11] varies from
144 to 15 to 78 N/mm for excursions of -2.54, 0, and +2.54 mm. From the P2 flexure modeling [RD15], the values are 158 to 24 to 76 N/mm for excursions of -2.55, 0, and +2.55 mm (and 109 to 24 to 56 N/mm for -1.95, 0, +1.95 mm). For the minimum value, we round to zero. For the maximum value, we use the largest value (we don’t add additional margin here because of the margin in the actuator range-of-travel budget and the strong dependence of spring constant on excursion), yielding a range of 0 to 55 N/mm per actuator.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1040] The actuator shall meet all performance requirements in the presence of a guide flexure whose effective axial stiffness per actuator varies from 0 N/mm to 55 N/mm. [REQ-2-M1CS-0800]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1100] The actuator shall meet all performance requirements over a range of in-plane motion of the mirror segment with respect to the fixed frame of +/- 0.5 mm and tilts of +/- 0.1 deg, including accommodation of installation errors onto the fixed frame. [REQ-2-M1CS-0820, -2400]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0904] The actuator encoder shall be collocated with the voice coil to a frequency of at least 200 Hz as mounted on a rigid base and with a non-dynamical load. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]
Discussion: The homing error is part of the SSA stroke budget; this value is a small fraction of that range.

Discussion: These two requirements are intended to allow use of the actuators for direct measurement of the actuator to edge sensor interaction matrix. They represent achievable values with standard optical encoders. The parent requirement is the PSSN for “Segment Dynamic Displacement Residual, which assumes a well calibrated A-matrix.
Discussion: The in-plane and tip/tilt ranges are described in REQ-1-OAD-1725 and -1735. These are conservative, as they apply to the PSA and the mirror cell.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1220] The actuator encoder shall have a positioning accuracy of 10 micron rms over the full range of travel with respect to the achieved home position. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]
Discussion: This requirement is to ensure minimum phase response out to the frequency at which the actuator is gain stable.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1200] The actuator shall have a homing repeatability of better than 25 microns, with or without an attached load. [REQ-2-M1CS-2400, -2200]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1000] The actuator shall meet all performance requirements with an axial load ranging from 65 to 830 N. [REQ-2-M1CS-0800]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6220] The actuator shall include a provision to be moved manually in the event of failure
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1240] The actuator encoder shall have a relative positioning accuracy of 100 nm rms over any 20 micron interval with the full range of travel. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]

Discussion: This would be accommodated with a knob on the snubber motor, accessible inside the cover. Note that the actuator can be removed from the telescope in any state, as the connection to the moving frame is via a clamped interface.
Discussion: The value of the reflected mass of the actuator plays a role in the control design and system modeling. The reflected mass in the POC voice actuator is approximately 45 kg.

Discussion: Requirements REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6300, -6400, and -6500 are placeholders for now, and will be refined in the context of an overall M1CS RMA plan. 2 yrs corresponds to the segment recoating cycle: ideally, any required actuator servicing would be done as part of this process. 30 min per actuator on this cycle corresponds to 0.2 FTE allocated for this function.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6300] The actuator preventive maintenance interval shall not be more frequent than every 2 yr (TBC). [REQ-2-M1CS-4180]

Discussion: The current allocation for M1CS actuators in the observatory downtime budget, REQ-1-OAD-0332, is 0.48%, part of 0.73% for all of M1CS per REQ-1-OAD-0328. The actual value will likely need refining as part of an overall M1CS availability plan.

Discussion: This requirement affects wind rejection; see the discussion at the beginning of this section (3.4.3). This stiffness is higher than that achievable on the telescope with a servo design that accommodates CSI, and serves to ensure that CSI, and not the actuator, will limit the stiffness at this frequency.Discussion: This requirement affects wind rejection; see the discussion at the beginning of this section (3.4.3). This stiffness is higher than that achievable on the telescope with a servo design that accommodates CSI, and serves to ensure that CSI, and not the actuator, will limit the stiffness at this frequency.
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-7500] The actuator shall not emit light outside of its enclosure. [REQ-2-M1CS-0520]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-7400] The actuators shall comply with fault, interlock, and emergency stop monitoring and control in a manner consistent with the TMT Observatory Hazard Analysis document. [REQ-2-M1CS-0452]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6000] The actuator shall be designed to operate and meet all requirements for 50 years with preventive maintenance. [REQ-2-M1CS-4210]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1110] The actuator shall meet all functional requirements over a range of in-plane motion of the mirror segment with respect to the fixed frame of +/- 1 mm and tilts of +/- 0.1 deg, including accommodation of installation errors onto the fixed frame. [REQ-2-M1CS-0840, -2400]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-7520] The actuator shall not emit electromagnetic radiation that would interfere with or degrade the performance of systems or subsystems at the observatory. [REQ-2-M1CS-0560]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-7530] The actuator shall be capable of operating in an environment with TBD levels of EMI/RFI interference. [REQ-2-M1CS-0580]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6100] The actuator reliability shall meet the allocation for actuator availability in the M1CS availability budget. [REQ-2-M1CS-4020, -4040]

Discussion: We assume that the replacement actuator is pre-configured off the telescope first. See also REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1210, which addresses the ability to set the zero point without requiring the SCC.

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-1210] The actuator shall have provision, either through a hardware feature or a procedure, such that it can be installed so that the actuator range of travel is centered on the SSA range of travel to within 0.25 mm without the need for power at the segment. [REQ-2-M1CS-2400, -2200]

[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6200] The actuator shall be designed such that it can be removed from the SSA and replaced in 15 minutes by personnel working in the mirror cell with the telescope pointing to the zenith. [REQ-2-M1CS-4140]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-0865] Soft actuator only: The actuator offload compliance shall be 200,000 N/m +/- 30%. [REQ-2-M1CS-3000]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6400] The actuator preventive maintenance shall take not longer than 30 min (TBC) per actuator. [REQ-2-M1CS-4180]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-6500] Each actuator shall be uniquely identifiable via TBD mechanism. [REQ-2-M1CS-4180]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-7540] The actuator shall be sealed to prevent any particulate contamination to either themselves or the environment. REQ-2-M1CS-0400]
[REQ-3-M1CS.ACT-7560] Any lubrication used inside the actuator shall be contained to prevent contamination. [REQ-2-M1CS-0400]

OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000735__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf

M1CS maintains the mirror shape in the presence of slow disturbances attributable to changing temperature and telescope elevation angle (gravity vector), as well as dynamic disturbances from wind and vibration sources. The setpoints of the M1CS are determined by the Alignment and Phasing System (APS), which is run every 2−4 weeks after a segment exchange, augmented by optical feedback from the acquisition, guiding, and wavefront sensor system (AGWFS) or the Adaptive Optics system (AO). Control of M1CS is coordinated by the Telescope Control System (TCS).

The M1CS is one of several systems that maintain the shape and/or position of the primary, secondary, and tertiary mirrors of TMT, as shown schematically in ‘Figure: Conceptual View of the control of the TMT telescope optics’. Hierarchically, M1CS is one level below the TCS, as shown schematically in ‘Figure: Telescope control hierarchy'.
Figure. Conceptual model of the Thiry Meter Telescope.

Figure. Conceptual view of the control of the TMT telescope optics. M1CS, part of the M1 System, is one of several systems that maintains the shape and/or position of TMT's primary (M1), secondary (M2), and tertiary (M3) mirrors.

Figure. Telescope control hierarchy. M1CS has an interface with TCS, which controls the high level behavior of M1CS. M1CS also has interfaces (either direct, or mediated by TCS) with APS, AGWFS, and AO.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000728__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
The major components of M1CS are [REQ-1-OAD-0179]:

Sensors
The edge sensors are used to measure the relative positions of each of the 492 segments of TMT. The sensors are mounted on the back side of the segments, with two sensor halves on each inter-segment edge: 2772 pairs, total. The sensors, coupled with electronic readouts, measure on one output the sum of the relative segment height difference and dihedral angle, and on the other output the gap between the segments. A dry gas purge system and a sensor boot keep the sensor clean and dry.

Actuators
The actuators are used to position each of the 492 segments in piston, tip, and tilt: 1476 actuators, total. The actuators are mounted between the fixed and moving frames of the Primary Segment Assemblies (PSAs) on the telescope. The actuators incorporate a local sensor and a high-rate servo to meet their requirements.

Segment Controller & Cabling (SCC)
The SCC provides distributed electronics, networking, and power to all of the segment actuators and edge sensors, and interfaces to the Global Loop Controller (GLC). The SCC also controls the forces applied by the 21 warping harnesses (part of the PSA) on each segment as determined by APS, and provides segment temperature sensors. Most of the SCC hardware is attached to the telescope. In the reference implementation, actuator and sensor control are local to each segment. On the telescope structure, there are 84 node boxes, each of which consolidates the networking for up to 6 segments, as well as 6 sector boxes, and one mirror box.

Global Loop Controller (GLC)
The GLC implements the M1CS control algorithms; provides overall system control, calibration, configuration, diagnostics, and other executive functions; and provides an engineering interface. In addition to software, the GLC includes a computer in the observatory computer room.

Each of these four components has its own DRD (RD1), (RD2), (RD3), (RD4), with requirements that flow from this document. 'Figure: Schematic view of the M1CS components on the telescope' is a schematic view of the M1CS components and their relationships on the telescope.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000729__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
Figure. Schematic view of the M1CS components on the telescope. (Coolant is shown, although it may not be required).
M1CS receives inputs from TCS for high level subsystem control and configuration. M1CS also receives configuration inputs on segment installation status as required to configure its control loop.
Figure. M1CS: normal operations.

During alignment, illustrated in Figure below titled 'M1CS: Under APS control (direct commanding path)', APS commands the segment positions via M1CS to align M1. This alignment process (an “APS run”) is repeated at different telescope elevations and temperatures, for which the in-plane positions of the segments will vary. The raw sensor heights and gaps for each of the APS runs, corresponding to a well-aligned telescope, are stored in the database. M1CS can also receive commands from APS (or TCS) to control the segment warping harnesses.

During normal operation, as illustrated in Figure below titled 'Figure: M1CS: normal operations', M1CS uses a set of edge sensor calibration coefficients stored in the local observatory database. These calibration coefficients include the sensor zero points, as well as the coefficients for terms proportional to sensor gap and shear, and possibly other parameters, to correct the raw edge sensor readings to account for segment in-plane motion and other effects. M1CS uses these corrected sensor heights as inputs to the global loop controller. M1CS also receives from TCS the PTT target, and low-order optical feedback from the AGWFS or the AO system.
Figure. M1CS: Under APS control (direct commanding path).
Reference documents contain information complementing, explaining, detailing, or otherwise supporting the information included in the current document.
Figure. Offline calibration coefficient update.

On demand, as illustrated in Figure titled 'Figure: Offline calibration coefficient update', the raw sensor data are processed to update the sensor calibration coefficients. The sensor calibration module performs this function. It will be provided by M1CS, although it may be later incorporated into TCS.

The Primary Mirror Control System (M1CS) is responsible for the real-time control of the segmented Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) primary mirror (M1). ‘Figure: Conceptual Model of the Thiirty Meter Telescope’ shows a conceptual model of TMT, illustrating the segmentation of the primary mirror. The primary mirror is 30 m in diameter, and consists of 492 hexagonal segments measuring 1.44 m corner-to-corner (1.24 m face-to-face), with a 2.5 mm gap between segments.
M1CS returns status, health, and event data; logs performance and diagnostic telemetry; and maintains the M1CS configuration in the local observatory database.

This subsection lists the interfaces between the M1CS and other subsystems with which it must be compatible. Each interface has a reference to a corresponding ICD. See [REQ-1-OAD-0100] and the TMT Interface N^2 Diagram (AD4). Not all of these will have an ICD per se. For example, the interface to observatory software will probably be more of compliance to an interface spec. Current ICDs are given in (AD5), (AD6), (AD7), (AD8), (AD9), (AD10), and (AD11).
In addition, the following interfaces, not identified in the N2 diagram, may be required:

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_280000072e__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_280000072f__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
A schematic of the M1CS control function is shown in 'Figure: Functional schematic of M1CS control'.

The primary function of the M1CS is to maintain the shape of the primary mirror. The shape is reconstructed from the corrected readings of the segment edge sensors (and the actuator positions for piston, tip, and tilt). Feedback to the segment actuators maintains the mirror shape in the presence of quasistatic (temperature, gravity) and dynamic (wind, vibration) disturbances, with control bandwidths of 1–2 Hz for the highest order mirror shape modes. M1CS, via the TCS Corrections Module, also makes use of real time optical measurements made by AGWFS or the AO system.

M1CS also implements several quasistatic control functions, including commanding of the segment warping harness in response to requests from TCS or APS, and logs segment temperature readings. M1CS includes calibration and configuration functions as needed for the control implementation, as well as diagnostic and monitoring functions.

Figure. Functional schematic of M1CS control. The items in green indicate the components of M1CS, including the GLC, which communicate via the SCC with the edge sensors, actuators, and segment temperature sensors (part of SCC). These latter items are attached to the primary segment assemblies, which include the segment warping harnesses that the SCC also controls. The GLC’s command interface is with TCS, and it implements both high and low bandwidth control of M1.

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: This subsection summarizes key factors constraining the design of the M1CS.

This subsection summarizes key factors that affect the requirements stated in this document. These factors are not design constraints on the system per se; however, any changes to them can affect the requirements.
The observatory must comply with local and national standards relevant to its construction and operation. [REQ-1-ORD-1005]
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_280000072a__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
The M1CS includes a number of interfaces to other subsystems. Changes to these other subsystems may affect M1CS requirements.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_280000077a__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf

The M1CS will operate as an autonomous subsystem of TCS, which provides high-level command and configuration. M1CS will provide status information of its operation and health, reporting any malfunction in the subsystem as a whole, or problems with its components. M1CS also includes an expert user interface.

The planned TMT lifetime is 50 years. Components must generally be designed to last at least 50 years, and may require preventive maintenance programs to meet the lifetime requirement. Electronics will likely not last 50 years and should comply with common standards in order to facilitate upgrades over the course of observatory operation. [REQ-1-ORD-1000]

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.SE_Notes: 20150817 (ACM) Change in no of segments exchanges per work day WAS 8 IS 10; OPSRD appendices.
IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: TMT has requirements for very high availability, and so limited time is built into the TMT operations schedule for nighttime calibration, and the downtime budget allocation for the M1CS is tight. The scheduled night time allocated for post-segment-exchange alignment and phasing (used to calibrate M1) is 93 hours per year spread over 31 three-hour events (OPSRD Appendix A (RD19)). The scheduled day time allocated to segment exchange is 8 hours/day, 31 days/year, with 10 segments exchanged in each work day (OPSRD Appendix B (RD19)). M1CS disconnection, connection, and verification can take only a small fraction of this time.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_280000072b__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf

The M1CS has no sensors that directly measure the wavefront errors that it is tasked to correct. It operates using calibration coefficients determined from periodic measurements by APS, with feedback of low order modes from the AGWFS or AO systems. Changes to the operation and performance of APS, AGWFS, or AO will influence the operation and performance of M1CS.
Changes to the parent documents will result in changes to this document.

Discussion: The M1CS components on the fixed frame are the actuator electronics and the lower segment box.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0140] The M1CS components mounted on the segments of the PSAs shall dissipate to air less than 1.2 W/segment (TBC).

Discussion: The relevant components on this level are the node (84), sector (6), and M1 (1) boxes. Assuming the sector and M1 boxes have twice the consumption of the node boxes, the node boxes would dissipate ~20 W (TBC) each.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0160]The M1CS components mounted on the moving and fixed frames of the PSAs shall dissipate to air less than 12.0 W/segment (TBC) when the warping harnesses and strain guages are inactive.
Discussion: The values in requirements 0140, 0160, and 0200 come from the 8/24/10 heat release study update (RD8), page 5: “Heat load configuration, August reduced.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0200] The M1CS components on the mirror cell, excluding the PSAs, shall dissipate to air less than 2 kW (TBC).
Discussion: This is the total power dissipated to air, subject to the maximums by level given above.
Discussion: The parent also specifies that the full load is attached to UPS and to the backup generator.
Discussion: Preferably, no glycol cooling will be necessary.
Discussion: The parent also specifies that the full load is attached to UPS and to the backup generator.
The downtime attributable to M1CS is 0.73% of the operating time. [REQ-1-OAD-0328]
[REQ-2-M1CS-0210] The total power dissipated to water-glycol by the telescope-mounted M1CS components shall be less than 2.5 kW.
Discussion: The M1CS components on moving frame are the sensor support electronics and the warping harness electronics (demand power only).

The requirements stated in this document flow down from requirements in the OAD (RD18), ORD (RD17), and OPSRD (RD19). In particular, changes in the assumptions about the disturbance environment will impact the error budget terms which apply to M1CS.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0100] The total mass of the telescope-mounted components of the M1CS shall be less than 29,100 kg (TBR).
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000734__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
[REQ-2-M1CS-0240] The total power used by the telescope-mounted M1CS components shall be less than 12.5 kW (TBR) of AC power.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0220] The peak load used by the M1CS equipment located in the observatory computing facilities shall be less than 1.5 kW (TBR) of AC power.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000397__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf

Table. Environmental constraints.
Discussion: We assume that this requirement does not apply to the M1CS computer in the computer room: typical servers are only rated down to +5C.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0230] The M1CS equipment located in the observatory computing facilities shall be air cooled.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000731__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
Discussion: The dust environment has not been specified. However based on Keck data and experience, the sensors will require boots.
Discussion: When the warping harnesses are driven or read back – infrequently – the instantaneous power will exceed this value.
Discussion: [REQ-1-ORD-2915] relates to the degradation of the mirror coatings from dust accumulation, and is the closest parent: we don’t want M1CS to produce additional contamination.
Discussion: The M1CS electronics boxes will also include utility networking for the mirror cell; in principle this should have a separate power allotment.
IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.SE_Notes: 20150817 (ACM) Added power.

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: [REQ-2-M1CS-0400] The M1CS component shall be sufficiently sealed to prevent particulate contamination of the telescope optics.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0410] The M1CS, in any installed state, shall be designed to withstand repeated exposure to the environmental conditions in Table above titled 'Table: Environmental constraints', Column (D) without damage.
Discussion: This is a “frequent earthquake.” “The levels of a 10-year return period earthquake have a 10% probability of being exceeded in a one year period.”
Discussion: This is an “infrequent earthquake.” “The levels of a 200-year return period earthquake have a 22% probability of being exceeded in a 50 year period.”
[REQ-2-M1CS-0250] The total power dissipated to air by the telescope-mounted M1CS components shall be less than 10.0 kW when the warping harnesses and strain gauges are inactive.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0420] The M1CS, in any installed state, shall survive earthquakes up to the levels of the 10-year return period earthquake with no damage. This corresponds to peak accelerations on the mirror cell of 0.5 g.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0425] After exposure to an earthquake up to the levels of the 200-year return period earthquake, once the observatory staff has resumed regular duty, the M1CS shall be able to resume normal operations within two weeks using spares that are on-site, the available staff, and normally available equipment. This corresponds to peak accelerations on the mirror cell of 1.8 g.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0427] The telescope-mounted M1CS components shall be designed to not violate their interface requirements under the loads resulting from an earthquake up to the levels of the 1000-year return period earthquake. This corresponds to peak accelerations on the mirror cell of 3 g.

Discussion: This is the parent for actuator requirements on hard stops and the snubber. Some constraint of the PSA motion is required to avoid segment to segment contact when the telescope is subject to earthquake loads.

Discussion: Many of the M1CS components will not be readily accessible after installation (e.g. actuator internals, electronic components, and cabling). The M1CS should have self-test modes to check components that can’t be verified through visual inspection. See also [REQ-2-M1CS-0412].

Discussion: The above requirement is a restatement of [REQ-1-ORD-1425] as applied to the M1CS. This is written so that it doesn’t have to be updated if we add an interface. M1CS can’t really test what will happen at the observatory level if power goes down, but we can test what we do at interfaces when power goes down. If the interfaces are well defined for power on and off states, then the statement in [REQ-2-M1CS-0460] is sufficient.
Discussion: Currently the daytime allocation in the OAD is lower: 0.8 kW. We do not expect a daytime/nighttime difference, and this needs to be resolved.

Discussion: The 0.5 g value is approximate, and is derived by scaling the value in REQ-2-M1CS-0425 per Figure 5‑22 in (RD10). This requirement is not driving, given the much higher levels in the next two requirements.
Discussion: Glycol cooling is available if more power is required than can be dissipated to air; see [REQ-2-M1CS-0210].
[REQ-2-M1CS-0340] The M1CS shall meet its performance requirements over the environmental range shown in 'Table: Environmental constraints', Column (B).

Discussion: While the OAD doesn’t specify a range of RH, it states that condensing conditions correspond to a dew point depression of 2 deg. At 25C, this corresponds to a RH of 85% – less at lower temperatures – and we adopt this value for columns (B) and (C).

Discussion: The 3 g value comes from [REQ-1-OAD-1287], which gives the limits on dynamic accelerations allowed by the structure. Note that accelerations beyond this value can occur at the segment due to the non-linear behavior of the snubber.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0412] The M1CS shall be designed such that if the conditions described in [REQ-2-M1CS-0410] or [REQ-2-M1CS-0420] occur, it shall be possible to perform a functional check in less than 6 hours.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0300] The telescope-mounted equipment of the M1CS shall remain functional at a level to allow servicing to be conducted, over the environmental range shown in Table above titled 'Table: Environmental Constraints', Column (C).
Discussion: This requirement limits the peak force applied to the segment due to the non-linear behavior the snubber, and sets the actuator-to-PSA interface loads.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0434] The peak accelerations propagated through the M1CS actuators to the segments shall be less than 5 g and 6 g for the 200-year and 1000-year return period earthquakes.
Deleted: Discussion: At the highest level, the parents are the high-level requirements regarding damage to optics for the 1000 yr earthquake, REQ-1-ORD-1560, REQ-1-ORD-1565.
IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.SE_Notes: 20150817 (ACM) Deleted

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: [REQ-2-M1CS-0430] The M1CS actuators shall have limits to constrain the maximum PSA motion.
Discussion: This requirement also covers the case of an E-Stop implementation that disables SCC power.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0440] The M1CS shall be designed such that its components can be readily self-tested and/or visually inspected for damage after earthquakes.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0460] The M1CS shall be designed such that single or multiple loss of power will not cause damage to itself or cause it to violate any of its interface requirements.

Discussion: See (RD11) and (RD12) for the analysis and testing supporting these adopted values. These values correspond to factors of safety of 1.5 and 1.25 applied to the 7.6 g buckling limit of the PSA flexures.

Discussion: These two requirements are placeholders for traceable disturbance profiles to be used in verifying compliance with REQ-2-M1CS-3000. There is no parent for the wind profile. The parent placeholder in the OAD for the vibration profile specifies a TBD spectral response. Note that vibration (and wind) response is already included in REQ-2-M1CS-3000.

Discussion: The ORD requirements are worded in terms of damage to optics or hazard to personnel. The wording for the M1CS requirement corresponds to M1CS components not damaging components to which they may be attached, including optics. An earthquake of this level could result in extensive damage to the M1CS components.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0520] M1CS components located in the telescope enclosure shall not emit light into the telescope enclosure environment.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0540] M1CS components located in the telescope enclosure shall meet all requirements under all ambient light conditions.
Discussion: In practice, we may simply require that there be no fans in the SCC components on the telescope.

Discussion: This requirement needs to be quantified and should probably be based on some industrial or consumer EMI standard (there are standards referenced in some of the parent docs). This is the corollary to [REQ-2-M1CS-0560]. The implications of this are mostly on SCC sensor electronics and synchronization.

Discussion: This is a restatement of [REQ-1-ORD-7410], as applied to the M1CS. This needs to be replaced with a reference to some kind of EMI standard to be testable. It is not anticipated the M1CS will be a significant source of EMI compared to the large telescope and enclosure drives.
Discussion: This requirement does not preclude, e.g., the use of optical encoders in the actuator, as long as there is an actuator enclosure.

Discussion: This addresses primarily the electronics of the SCC. Field connectors refers to external connectors to a component, which could be mated/demated on the telescope, vs. internal connectors, which would only be mated/demated in a laboratory or test environment. Accessible electronics interface points would include the sensor front-end electronics or other locations where ESD could be introduced during handling on the telescope. Depending on whether the component is commercial or custom, appropriate ESD specifications could include HBM +/-15 kV (RD14) or IEC 61000-4-2 (RD15).
[REQ-2-M1CS-0590] Components of the M1CS with field connectors or accessible electronic interface points shall be designed to be ESD resistant at those ports.

Discussion: The telescope must be able to observe anywhere on the sky from 1 to 65 deg zenith angle. As the segments follow the curvature of the primary mirror, the actuator tilt varies across the mirror. As the actuators are mounted parallel to the segment normal, for the 30 m circumscribed telescope diameter and a face-to-face segment diameter of 1.24 m, the maximum effective actuator radius is 14.4 m. For a 60 m ROC, actuators at the edge are canted in by a maximum angle of 14 deg, i.e., at a zenith angle of up to 79 deg. (An exact calculation from the segmentation database with the proper conic constant gives 13.4 deg.)
[REQ-2-M1CS-0800] The M1CS shall meet all performance requirements when the telescope is tilted at any zenith angle from 1° to 65°.
Discussion: Because of the curvature of the primary mirror, these correspond to a zenith angle range of 0 to 104 deg for the segment normals.
Discussion: In practice, the OAD parent is a requirement on the telescope structure. For performance calculations, M1CS will use the in-plane motion computed using the merit function routine (RD7).
[REQ-2-M1CS-0820] The M1CS shall meet all performance requirements in the presence of up to 0.5 mm in-plane relative motion of adjacent segments.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0840] The M1CS shall support servicing and maintenance over telescope zenith angles from -1 to +90 degrees.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0860] The M1CS shall support servicing and maintenance in the presence of up to 1.0 mm in-plane relative motion of adjacent segments.

Discussion: [REQ-1-ORD-1800] requires that “Within 3 minutes, the telescope and enclosure shall be able to point from any one position on the sky to any other in a way ensuring the uninterrupted execution of the next observation, and settle control loops and structural dynamics sufficiently to be ready for object acquisition.” [REQ 1-OAD-1376] and [REQ-1-OAD-1378] define telescope azimuth and elevation velocity and accelerations equivalent to a maximum slew time of 2 minutes in azimuth and 1 minute in elevation. [REQ-1-ORD-1805] requires that both pointing and acquisition are complete in 5 min.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0866] The M1CS shall be able to track at elevation rates up to 15.5 deg/hr.

Discussion: The 30 s (TBC) value allows for closing (if opened for the slew) and settling of the local actuator loop and the global loop; M1CS slew rate requirements are addressed in [REQ-2-M1CS-0872]. The requirement applies after the mount control has settled to TBD accuracy.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0870] The M1CS shall be able to stabilize M1 to allow object acquisition in less than 30 s (TBC) after conclusion of a telescope slew of any amount and after MCS has settled to less than TBD milliarcsec.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0490] M1CS shall meet its performance requirements subject to TBD vibration disturbance profile. [REQ-1-OAD-2105]

Discussion: We adopt this requirement to support [REQ-2-M1CS-0870] and simplify operations. The velocity and acceleration values are those given in the structure DRD (RD9): [REQ-2-STR-1030] and [REQ-2-STR-1010]. [REQ-1-OAD-0800] defines a maximum actuator travel for gravity deformations of 1.8 mm. Thus, these imply an actuator position slew rate of approximately 30 um/s.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0480] M1CS shall meet its performance requirements subject to TBD wind disturbance profile.
Discussion: This does not include the time to close the local actuator loop (if opened for the slew): that is accounted for in [REQ-2-M1CS-0870].
Discussion: In practice, the OAD parent is a requirement on the telescope structure.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0872] The M1CS shall be able to slew to the position of a new target by the conclusion of a telescope elevation slew at up to 1 deg/s and 0.1 deg/s2.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0874] The M1CS shall be able to stabilize M1 to allow object acquisition in less than 1 s (TBC) after conclusion of a telescope slew of up to 5 arcmin and after MCS has settled to less than TBD milliarcsec.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0876] The M1CS shall be able to stabilize M1 to allow object acquisition in less than 2 s (TBC) after conclusion of a telescope slew of up to 1 deg and after MCS has settled to less than TBD milliarcsec.

Discussion: There is presently no numbered requirement that this traces to, but it does link to the maintenance time budget in the OPSRD, Appendix B (RD19). With an OPSRD budget of 10 segments in one workday, this M1CS requirement would require half time of one person dedicated to M1CS during segment exchange.

Discussion: This is a requirement on keeping mechanical, electrical, and purge-system connections and disconnections simple, with straightforward procedures, and with connectors & interfaces that are simple to mate/demate. It also implies that electronic components are interchangeable, i.e., segments with different attached electronics are simply interchangeable. A self-test algorithm is specified in [REQ-2-M1CS-0960].
[REQ-2-M1CS-0880] The M1CS shall be designed to require less than 30 minutes (TBC) per segment of service time by a trained operator during a segment exchange.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0580] The M1CS shall be capable of operating in an environment with TBD levels of EMI/RFI interference.

Discussion: The large number of cables, combined with the altitude and temperature of the working environment, makes it important that cables are designed to prevent incorrect mating that could cause damage. This requirement flows from the maintenance time budget in the OPSRD, like [REQ-2-M1CS-0880].

Discussion: Per [REQ-1-OAD-0179], coolant will be provided through the telescope structure. We adopt this requirement on cooling of PSA components to simplify segment exchanges. Cooling of node boxes – not mounted on the PSAs – is allowed.

Discussion: The self-test function will typically be executed by a segment exchange crew to verify that all segment components are working properly at completion. The time required to conduct this test is included in the allocation for [REQ-2-M1CS-0880].
[REQ-2-M1CS-0920] The M1CS design shall use connectors that mechanically prevent incorrect mating of different types of cables.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0940] M1CS components mounted on the PSA shall not require coolant.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0960] The M1CS shall have a function that can be used to verify that individual M1CS components are operating correctly after a segment exchange.

Discussion: CO2 snow cleaning of M1 is a requirement. In-situ washing of M1 [REQ-1-OAD-1670] is a goal. Because of the proximity of the edge sensors to the optical surface, and their sensitivity to contamination, M1CS will only accommodate CO2 cleaning.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0980] All telescope-mounted M1CS components shall be designed to be compatible with in-situ CO2 cleaning of M1.

Discussion: This is to simplify the segment recoating process, so that components do not need to be removed. Because of the plan to differentially pump the PSA (i.e., seal the segment edge; high-vacuum pump on the “clean” front volume; medium-vacuum pump on the “dirty” back volume), UHV compatibility is not required, although virtual leaks should be avoided. Rather, the concern is more that the component properties be stable subject to short exposures to vacuum. For example, cable insulation should not exhibit high mass loss under vacuum. Given that all 492 segments are nominally recoated on a two-year schedule (OPSRD Appendix B (RD19)), the total time at vacuum will be small.

Discussion: It is not practical for M1CS components to be compatible with direct exposure to the chemicals and materials used for segment coating, stripping, and cleaning as part of the segment recoating process, and protection of M1CS components during these processes will be required. This may require an additional ICD with TMT.TEL.OPT (TBD).

Discussion: In addition to vacuum compatibility, the PSA-mounted M1CS components must be compatible with the temperature used for the coating process. There is no parent on the temperature, and we adopt 50°C for now. Note that significantly higher temperatures pose a risk to adhesives and polymers.

[REQ-2-M1CS-1000] All PSA-mounted M1CS components, including sensors, dust boots, SCC electronics, and SCC cables, must be compatible with a vacuum environment and temperature soaks to 50C as part of the segment recoating process.
Discussion: The two parents specifically apply to APS, but M1CS is required for APS to align M1, and should not be the limiting factor in the time required for the tasks.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0380] M1CS components that are dust-sensitive shall be protected by a boot or enclosure.
[REQ-2-M1CS-1040] M1CS shall be able to be commanded by APS to perform on-axis alignment in less than 30 minutes when all optics are within the alignment maintenance specifications. [REQ-1-OAD-2325]
[REQ-2-M1CS-1042] M1CS shall be able to be commanded by APS to perform on-axis alignment in less than 120 minutes when all optics are within the post segment exchange specifications. [REQ-1-OAD-2230]
[REQ-2-M1CS-2000] The M1CS shall control the out-of-plane degrees of freedom of each segment.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2020] The M1CS shall maintain the M1 global tip, tilt and piston using 3 actuators for each of the 492 mirror segments.

[REQ-2-M1CS-2040] The M1CS shall measure M1 segment position (gap, piston, and dihedral angle) relative to neighboring segments by means of 2772 sensors attached to all shared edges of the 492 segments.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2052] The M1CS shall maintain an interface with APS to enable alignment of M1.

Discussion: The 1.8 g value comes from [REQ-1-OAD-1287], which gives the limits on dynamic accelerations on the mirror cell. Note that accelerations beyond this value can occur at the segment due to the non-linear behavior of the actuator snubber.
Discussion: These coefficients are computed from data stored by M1CS in the observatory database. See the discussion for [REQ-2-M1CS-2070], below.

[REQ-2-M1CS-0500] The telescope-mounted equipment of the M1CS shall induce no more than 0.5 N rms vibration force on the telescope after passing through a filter that has unit magnitude over the frequency band f > 5 Hz to f < 20 Hz, decreasing as 1/f^2 below 5 Hz and f^2 above 20 Hz.
[REQ-2-M1CS-1020] All segment-mounted M1CS components shall be compatible with the segment recoating process.
Discussion: The OAD is not more specific than [REQ-2-M1CS-2060]; this requirement gives M1CS’s approach to sensor calibration.
Discussion: This corresponds to 1.1x sidereal at Mauna Kea (lat 19.82).
[REQ-2-M1CS-2050] The M1CS shall be controlled and configured by TCS.

Discussion: M1CS shall use these as inputs to an outer loop to drive the optical residuals to zero. The lowest order mode is astigmatism. See also [REQ-2-M1CS-2084] and [REQ-2-M1CS-2088]. We adopt 0.1 Hz as a requirement on M1CS.
[REQ-2-M1CS-0560] Components within the M1CS shall not emit electromagnetic radiation that would interfere with or degrade the performance of systems or subsystems at the observatory.

Discussion: M1CS shall command to this PTT target using feedback from the actuator encoders. An alternative implementation would be for TCS to give M1CS the parameters for an elevation-dependent lookup function for the PTT target. We adopt 0.1 Hz as a requirement on M1CS.
Discussion: M1CS shall use these as inputs to an outer loop to drive the optical residuals to zero, like for [REQ-2-M1CS-2080]. We adopt 0.1 Hz as a requirement on M1CS.

Discussion: We assume that M1CS provides a nominal routine to compute sensor calibration coefficients from sets of APS data – see the context diagrams in Sec. 2.2.1. This routine would be invoked by TCS, which would specify the APS runs to be used.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2080] The M1CS shall receive corrections from TCS, based on optical feedback, for Zernike modes of M1 up to the 6th radial order at up to 0.1 Hz.

Discussion: See the discussion for [REQ-2-M1CS-2070], above. In the proposed implementation, the sensor set point is included in the sensor calibration coefficients, such that this offset would nominally be zero during routine operation. We leave this hook in for flexibility in implementation and diagnostics. We adopt 1 Hz as a requirement on M1CS.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2070] The M1CS shall use sensor gap readings to correct the sensor height readings in the presence of in-plane motion.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2200] The M1CS shall be capable of aligning M1 for normal operation from any set of actuator positions without external input.

Discussion: This requirement ensured that the initial errors are within the range of APS. Note the 30 um surface value applies after APS corrects any tilt errors. Note that there are additional requirements on the initial segment shape which are not the responsibility of M1CS.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2100] The M1CS shall be able to receive sensor offsets from TCS at up 1 Hz (TBC) to which to control M1.

[REQ-2-M1CS-2220] The M1CS shall be capable of aligning each M1 segment to within +/- 30 microns (surface) and +/- 20 arcsec (sky; one-dimension) after a segment exchange and without any on-sky calibrations or alignments.

Discussion: This addresses operation during AIV as the mirror is built up, and during steady state where a segment may be missing, or uncontrolled due to an M1CS actuator, sensor, or electronics fault, or a PSA mechanical fault.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2300] The M1CS shall be able to function with uninstalled, removed, or uncontrolled mirror segments as limited by controllability and noise propagation.

Discussion: There is a high degree of sensor redundancy, so it will usually be possible to operate with a small number of sensors removed from the control to accommodate sensor faults. This is the experience from Keck. However, large numbers of missing sensors, or certain distributions of sensor faults, cannot be accommodated without loss of performance. Accurately quantifying this requirement would require very extensive modeling and simulations.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2320] The M1CS shall meet the performance requirements with as many as TBD edge sensors removed from the control loop subject to TBD constraints on their distribution.

Discussion: This is for APS functionality, and also to allow for destacking of segments due to segment or actuator faults (assuming at least one functional actuator). This range is easily achieved with the actuator stroke budget in [REQ-2-M1CS-2400]. With three actuators at a 531 mm radius, moving any one actuator by 1 mm tilts the segment by 1/(1.5 x 531) = 260 arcsec.

Discussion: Reconfiguration includes sensors and/or actuators from the control loop. Reconfiguration is most likely to be done in the event of a failed actuator or sensor. This may also include regeneration of a control matrix. The 3 minutes is TBC, but should be made consistent with the downtime allocations.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2280] The M1CS shall be able to tilt any uncontrolled segments at least 40 arcsec on the sky from the controlled segments.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2260] The M1CS reconfiguration to add or remove segments from the control loop shall take less than 3 minutes (TBC).

[REQ-2-M1CS-2345] M1CS shall be capable of meeting its performance requirements within 30 minutes (TBC) after starting from power-off with none of the electronics at their equilibrium operating temperatures.

Discussion: Requirement [REQ-1-OAD-9309] states that subsystems shall be able to initialize themselves to a default configuration and be ready for operation in less than one minute. Because of the extensive configuration that must be accessed from the local observatory database to configure the GLC, and the likely need to reestablish the actuator encoder zero points, it is not anticipated that the one minute requirement can be achieved.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2060] The M1CS shall use sensor calibration coefficients determined from multiple APS measurements.

[REQ-2-M1CS-2347] M1CS shall be capable of meeting its performance requirements within 5 minutes (TBC) of a warm restart (power cycle with electronics already at equilibrium operating temperatures) or soft restart (software restart without hardware power cycle).

Discussion: The requirement includes the error from mounting the sensor system to the segment and from inter-segment forces attributable to dust-boot operation. The intent during segment finishing is to install dummy sensors and to polish out any print-through to the optical surface. Thus the practical requirement on mounting is that mounting forces be repeatable, and the mass properties of the sensor and boot be repeatable. For dust boots contacting between segments, the maximum allowed force needs to be specified.
Discussion: Per the OAD, the TCS Corrections Module is responsible for maintaining the M1 shape lookup table [REQ-1-OAD-0173] using APS measurements.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000411__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
Discussion: See Table 12 in (RD18) for suballocations.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2390] The sensor components mounted on the segment of the PSA shall comply with the edge-sensor to optics ICD in order to control their contribution to segment figure.
OLE_AB_5051efba363412fb_23_21000000aa_2800000412__9c0be7b1-05f7-432e-972c-aaf3c5f411ee_OBJECTTEXT_0.rtf
Discussion: We use the same parent as for [REQ-2-M1CS-2300], absent a specific robustness spec or reduced-performance budget; see the discussion for [REQ-2-M1CS-4040].
[REQ-2-M1CS-2400] The actuators shall have a 5.0 mm range of travel.
Deleted: Table 2. Actuator range of travel budget from the OAD.
IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.SE_Notes: 20150818 (ACM) Deleted

IMCE_profle_adaption_for_TMT_:TMT_Requir.Text: Discussion: The M1CS (after calibration) should be able to bring the M1 into alignment for operation from an arbitrary set of actuator positions. Specifically, the sensors need to have the correct sign of the error over the uncertainty range of the segment pistons.

Discussion: The warping harnesses and sensors are part of M1. The current M1 design concept includes a dead-zone in the warping harness mechanism in order to establish the zero point of the strain gauges. We assume that M1 will provide the initialization algorithm that M1CS will implement.

Discussion: Sensor calibration for TMT is more complicated than for Keck. At Keck, the sensor targets consist of a setpoint for each sensor determined from a single APS run plus an offset from an elevation lookup table derived from multiple APS runs over time to account for gravity sag of the system. For TMT, it is necessary to correct the sensor height readings for the in-plane motion of the sensors. These corrections use a model that depends on sensor gaps, the coefficients of which are solved for using APS measurements at different elevation angles and temperatures to span a range of in-plane motions. Note that since the sensor calibration depends on APS runs which could be taken weeks apart; and that on segment exchange we don’t wish to discard the in-plane calibrations of the unchanged segments – rather, to refine them, gradually deweighting older APS data – the operational aspects of the problem are complicated.

Discussion: The exact rate is not specified in the parent. As there are 10,000 stepper motors, the electronics are demand-only, and there are total power dissipation requirements which will limit the number of motors which can be energized at any one time, the specific use case needs to be defined.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2430] The M1CS shall implement a provided initialization function to establish the zero point of the warping harnesses.
Discussion: Per REQ-1-OAD-0179, M1 shape lookup table management is a TCS responsibility, and we delete old requirements 2120 and 2140.
Discussion: Update rates of 0.1 Hz for [REQ-2-M1CS-2080], [REQ-2-M1CS-2084], and [REQ-2-M1CS-2088] would allow closed-loop bandwidths of approximately 0.005 Hz.
[REQ-2-M1CS-2460]The M1CS shall read out all warping harness strain gauges upon request from APS or TCS within 30 s (TBC).

Discussion: The parent requirements are stated in terms of telescope moves being completed in 1.5 s and 5 s for 5 arcmin and 1 degree moves, resp. For commensurate M1CS settling times (not specified in the parents), M1CS must remain linear. In particular, for the current actuator concept, the actuators much accommodate the move without use of their offloaders, and integrator windup in the global loop must be controlled. Because of noise propagation and CSI accommodation, the lowest order mirror modes of M1 may be controlled with servo bandwidths of 0.25 Hz, and the settling time of these modes will dominate the settling of M1CS. The 1 s and 2 s (TBC) values for the 1 arcmin and 1 deg moves correspond to settling times of ~2.5 and ~5 time constants, resp. These settling times apply after the mount control has settled to TBD accuracy.
Discussion: The exact rate is not specified in the parent. As there are 10,000 strain gauges, and the electronics are demand-only, the specific use case needs to be defined.

Discussion: Note that the likely implementation of the warping harness drivers and signal conditioners by M1CS will completely disable them when not in use to meet power dissipation requirements. Thus, drive power cannot be used to maintain warping harness position, and sensor positions will only be available on request (rather than continuously - we delete old requirement 2440). This is consistent with the M1 design concept that uses stepper motors to maintain position without power, and uses strain gauges (an absolute sensor).

Discussion: We specify at level 2 – this document – the focus-mode sensing approach and adopted Leff. Discussion: REQ-1-OAD-8615 currently specifies a focus offload bandwidth of 0.0001 Hz, i.e., quasistatic. However, a significantly higher bandwidth is required for M1CS to meet its error budget allocation given plausible assumptions on sensor systematic errors. In particular, while ~4 nm correlated sensor error leads to a PSSN degradation attributable to focus mode of ~0.002 with secondary refocus, the sensor correlated error allocation becomes ~0.25 nm without secondary refocus; we do not believe this smaller allocation is achievable.
